public_rationale: The claim says a system that cannot maintain cognitive models of the world cannot reason reliably, however much memory or compute it has. The source gives no test, threshold or deadline. The resolution contract says neither 'reason reliably' nor 'maintain cognitive models of the world' has an agreed operational definition, and that whether a given system has world models is disputed. A claim that holds 'no matter how much compute' cannot be confirmed by a finite number of experiments. Refuting it would first need agreement that a specific system lacks world models. The evidence packet lists two candidate papers, and neither was used. According to the packet's notes, one reports transformers failing at compositional reasoning and the other reports weak autonomous planning by LLMs in 2023. Neither tests whether world models are a necessary condition for reliable reasoning. So the claim cannot be scored against dated evidence.
limitations: No evidence item was used in this assessment.
The evidence does not establish whether any specific system has or lacks cognitive models of the world.
There is no agreed test for 'maintaining cognitive models of the world' or for 'reasoning reliably'.
Finite observations cannot check the claim's universal scope ('regardless of memory or compute').

our_interpretation: This is a general theoretical claim that maintaining world models is a necessary condition for reliable reasoning, at any scale.

No test, threshold, or deadline is given. 'Reason reliably' and 'maintain cognitive models of the world' have no agreed operational definitions, and whether a given system has world models is itself disputed.
A universal 'no matter how much compute' claim cannot be confirmed by finite experiments. Refuting it would first require agreement that some system lacks world models yet reasons reliably.
criteria.support_condition: Not adjudicable. Support would need an accepted way to tell whether a system maintains world models, plus evidence that every system lacking them fails at reliable reasoning at every scale.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not adjudicable. Contradiction would need agreement that a specific system lacks world models, plus evidence that it nonetheless reasons reliably.
